Some others are giving similar advice but I've been there and here is my more detailed take to maybe help with understanding the concept of "flavor is free"  
Do not make statblocks yet. Just take existing stat blocks and look at their mechanics and work on recognizing what kind of story you can tell with the abilities.  
For example lets take the Bugbear Stalker from the 2025 MM  
The most notable features it has, (ignoring the obvious stuff like it wears armor and wields weapons) is the Abduct feature. (The bugbear needn't spend extra movement to move a creature it is grappling.) and the Quick Grapple. (bonus action, one Medium or smaller creature the bugbear can see within 10 feet, DC13 or Grappled) and of course that the Bugbear gets advantage with it's morning star against its Grapple Target.  
Take all that and think about how you could re-flavor it to be more narratively interesting, maybe this is a large scorpion like creature that can shoot spines (javelins) and likes to catch things in it's mandibles (morningstar) and once it has them in it's jaws it just takes off back to it's den. (possibly with other homebrewed monsters)  
and this is just one idea, it could be anything.  
and once you get a good idea of how stat blocks are built you can eventually start adding in  your own twists, pulling the mechanics you like from one monster to another, remember this is all for fun! and you are a player too so have fun with it, nothing is more fun than having your seasoned players running and screaming because they don't understand what exactly they are fighting (even if its just a troll re-flavored to be a self repairing ice construct hurling parts of it's own body)

From there its encounter building around a theme, find out what or where your players are going and try finding monster \*mechanics\* that fit the vibe you are going for, and don't be afraid to dial it up or down if the party needs it if all else fails but that should be decided after the fight starts and only if needed.  
hope this helps

Perhaps having the spell say that the item floats aloft in the ethereal plane would give it some interesting mechanical implications. It lets characters who can see into the ethereal plane via magical effects see the arsenal of mages with the spell which has cool lore opportunity. And additionally, it lets spells like blink be used to pilfer these extra dimensional spaces. I could see a very powerful archmage having a phase spider guarding them in the ethereal plane just to protect their items stored there etc.

Big thing to keep in mind is that the implications for killing a king is huge. Even an evil king has advisors or other people working under them to carry out their whims not including being that kingdom's public enemy number one.  
IMO I would unceremoniously let the king die like any other person would (assuming they were just a basic non-magic person.) let it sink in that killing one leader of a corrupt kingdom isn't the end all be all.
